svg.title: Media Studio — Know what lives where.
svg.desc: Private files, transient state, model caches and optional logging have different lifecycles. Select components in the interactive explorer for implementation details.

g.text: Private files, transient state, model caches and optional logging have different lifecycles.

g.title: Manual media editing, playback, waveform and timeline controls, plus the copilot interface. Suitable canvas edits can stay in the browser; advanced operations upload selected media to the application host.
A private environment file or process variables configure session secrets, quality ceilings, local model services, memory and optional activity logging.
The application entry point loads private configuration, establishes file locations, saves projects, serves artifacts and applies public response guards. Four blueprints handle domain operations.
Application process memory owns background-job records, resource admission and managed model handles. This is a single-process architecture rather than a distributed queue.
g.text: Job status, threads and model handles

g.title: Uploads, processed artifacts, saved projects, memory databases and personal skills remain outside versioned source. Saved-project references protect media from age-based cleanup.
Downloaded model weights remain on disk for later inference, independently of managed in-memory model unloading.
Native tools inspect, transform, render and export media. Local system speech is a fallback when the optional neural voice packs are unavailable.
A separately started local service can provide structured planning and optional embeddings. Operators configure the endpoint and served model IDs; no specific model vendor is required.
An explicitly enabled activity logger falls back to a local CSV when PostgreSQL is unavailable or unconfigured.
When activity logging is explicitly enabled and database configuration is available, upload metadata can be written to PostgreSQL. The destination is operator-configured.

g.text: Trusted single-user deployment · no built-in accounts or per-user ownership boundary
